pr_title: drivers: nrf_clock_calibration: wait for sensor initialization
pr_body:
When using the RC clock source a periodic calibration is invoked that
involves reading from the die temperature sensor.  The code did not
protect against execution order that caused the periodic calibration
to be invoked before the temperature sensor was initialized.

Update the temperature sensor to detect that it has not been
initialized and so should reject attempts to fetch a reading.

Update the calibration code to do nothing when temperature reading
fails.

Fixes #20416

issue_context.title: sample: sensor: fxos8700 issues
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
After compiling the fxos8700 sample for the BBC Micro:bit  fails to boot with a fatal error.

The issue appears to be connected to an update to the nRF series die temperature sensing. (drivers: sensor: temp_nrf5: Code cleanup #17249). The 'blocking' aspects seem to create a interrupt deadlock.

I have not reaised a PR with changes as this has links to the nRF Clock Control Calibration;
```
config CLOCK_CONTROL_NRF_CALIBRATION_TEMP_DIFF
    int "Temperature change triggering calibration (in 0.25 degree units)"
    default 2
    depends on CLOCK_CONTROL_NRF_K32SRC_RC_CALIBRATION && CLOCK_CONTROL_NRF && !CLOCK_CONTROL_NRF_FORCE_ALT && CLOCK_CONTROL
    help
      Calibration is triggered if the temperature has changed by at least
      this amount since the last calibration.
```

The issue may only exist on the nrf51 series as am unable to test on other devices.

**To Reproduce**
Follow steps indicated described sample, which need to be updated to use the WEST tool.

**Expected behavior**
Works as expected as in v1.14

**Impact**
Showstopper as appears to effect multiple sensors

**Screenshots or console output**

> [00:00:00.000,976] [1B][1;31m<err> os:  xpsr:  0x61000000[1B][0m
> [1B][1;31m--- 3 messages dropped ---
> [1B][0m[00:00:00.001,037] [1B][1;31m<err> os: Faulting instruction address (r15/pc): 0x0000449a[1B][0m
> [00:00:00.001,098] [1B][1;31m<err> os: >>> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR 0: CPU exception on CPU 0[1B][0m
> [00:00:00.001,159] [1B][1;31m<err> os: Current thread: 0x20000774 (unknown)[1B][0m
> [00:00:00.040,344] [1B][1;31m<err> os: Halting system[1B][0m



**Additional context**
If i amend the temp_nrf.c code to remove the block, the application works (well it boots and allows the accelerometer to be read).

**\drivers\sensor\nrf5\temp_nrf5.c**

Original Code:
```
	r = clock_control_async_on(data->hfclk_dev, NULL, &clk_data);
	__ASSERT_NO_MSG(!r);

	k_sem_take(&data->device_sync_sem, K_FOREVER);

	r = clock_control_off(data->hfclk_dev, 0);
	__ASSERT_NO_MSG(!r);
```

Amended Code:
```
	nrf_temp_task_trigger(NRF_TEMP, NRF_TEMP_TASK_START);

	k_sem_take(&data->device_sync_sem, K_MSEC(10));
```

comments: The problem is with initialization order.  Both the FXOX8700 and the nrf5/temp_nrf5 driver are initialized at `CONFIG_SENSOR_INIT_PRIORITY` in that order.  The FXOS8700 driver initialization suspends while waiting on a semaphore for an I2C operation to complete, allowing the `measure_temperature()` function in `nrf_clock_calibration.c` to be invoked through the work queue before `temp_nrf5_init` function has initialized the temperature sensor.

Well, no, that was **a** problem.  [This site](https://tech.microbit.org/hardware/i2c/) shows three variants of the microbit; the FXOS8700 is on v1.5 variant 2, while mine is v1.5 variant 1 with an LSM303AGR.  So I can't confirm that the accelerometer works as the Zephyr board description is for an entirely different device.

Nonetheless, #20641 should fix it for people with variant 2 boards.

review_comments: It seems to be that leaving here will break calibration algorithm as state machine will stay with HF clock turned on and nothing started to change the state (no calibration or calibration timer active). When calibration initially starts then `calib_skip_cnt` is set to 0 to ensure that calibration will be performed in first attempt disregarding temperature measurement. Initial temperature measurement is used only to have value for next iteration to calculate diff. If temperature sensor does not return value, then it would be better to set temperature to some arbitrary value (something unrealistic like 150'C). That will result in additional calibration during next timeout due to temperature change.

I'm not going to try tricks with temperatures; instead I've updated it to reset `cal_state` to the state that it was in when the callback determined it was necessary to invoke `measure_temperature()`.  Does that work (for you; I've verified it works for the test)?  If not I'd rather reassign this to you so you get a solution you're willing to maintain.
